answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make cheap identities expensive by tying reputation to scarce, verifiable work. Think of trust as nectar: it is earned drop by drop, only when an agent completes auditable tasks that others can check. A single whisper of self-praise counts for nothing; only a long record of honest work lets an identity shine like an opal, graded by its facets of completed jobs. Newcomers start with tiny, low-value trades, and only after a sustained history do they unlock larger deals, so forging a thousand fakes would require a thousand real histories.
